source_text: Hinc igitur dirigimus praescriptionem, si dominus Christus Iesus apostolos misit ad praedicandum, alios non esse recipiendos praedicatores quam Christus instituit, quia nec alius patrem novit nisi filius et cui filius revelavit, nec aliis videtur revelasse filius quam apostolis quos misit ad praedicandum, utique quod illis revelavit. Quid autem praedicaverint, id est quid illis Christus revelaverit, et hic praescribam non aliter probari debere, nisi per easdem ecclesias quas ipsi apostoli condiderunt, ipsi eis praedicando tam viva, quod aiunt, voce quam per epistulas postea. Si haec ita sunt, constat perinde omnem doctrinam quae cum illis ecclesiis apostolicis matricibus et originalibus fidei conspiret veritati deputandam, id sine dubio tenentem quod ecclesiae ab apostolis, apostoli a Christo, Christus a deo accepit: omnem vero doctrinam de mendacio praeiudicandam quae sapiat contra veritatem ecclesiarum et apostolorum Christi et dei. Superest ergo, ut demonstremus, an haec nostra doctrina, cuius regulam supra edidimus, de apostolorum traditione censeatur, et ex hoc ipso, an ceterae de mendacio veniant. Communicamus cum ecclesiis apostolicis, quod nulla doctrina diversa. Hoc est testimonium veritatis.
thought_title: The Rule for Testing Doctrine by Apostolic Churches
orientation: Tertullian is laying down the legal objection that only the churches founded by the apostles can prove what Christ revealed to them.
pass_a_gloss: From here therefore we direct the legal objection: if the Lord Christ Jesus sent the apostles to preach, no other preachers are to be received than those whom Christ appointed, because no one has known the Father except the Son and the one to whom the Son has revealed him, and the Son does not seem to have revealed to others than to the apostles whom he sent to preach, namely what he revealed to them. But what they preached, that is what Christ revealed to them, I will also here prescribe that it ought not to be proved otherwise than through those same churches which the apostles themselves founded, they themselves preaching to them both by the living voice, as they say, and by letters afterwards. If these things are so, it is established that every doctrine which agrees with those apostolic churches, the mothers and originals of the faith, is to be assigned to the truth, holding without doubt what the churches received from the apostles, the apostles from Christ, Christ from God: but every doctrine is to be judged beforehand as from falsehood which savors against the truth of the churches and of the apostles of Christ and of God. It remains therefore that we demonstrate whether this doctrine of ours, whose rule we set forth above, is judged to be from the tradition of the apostles, and from this very thing, whether the others come from falsehood. We share communion with the apostolic churches, because no doctrine is different. This is the testimony of the truth.

choices.why: The glossary requires this rendering for the technical legal term.

choices.english: the mothers and originals of the faith
choices.why: Keeps the maternal metaphor and the legal sense of source documents; 'originals' preserves the idea of authoritative source.
Preserves the sensory metaphor of taste, which Tertullian uses to describe doctrinal character.
Keeps the legal force of a preliminary judgment, matching the legal objection theme.
Preserves the ecclesial sense of shared fellowship and common faith.

pass_b_english: From this point, then, I direct my legal objection. If the Lord Jesus Christ sent the apostles to preach, no other preachers are to be received than those whom Christ appointed. For no one knows the Father except the Son and the one to whom the Son has revealed him (Matthew 11:27). And the Son does not appear to have revealed him to any others than the apostles whom he sent to preach, preaching, of course, what he had revealed to them.

And what they preached, that is, what Christ revealed to them, should be proved, I will also maintain here, in no other way than through those same churches which the apostles themselves founded. They founded them by preaching to them both with the living voice, as they say, and afterward through letters.

If this is so, it is settled that every doctrine which agrees with those apostolic churches, the mothers and originals of the faith, is to be assigned to the truth. Such a doctrine undoubtedly holds what the churches received from the apostles, the apostles from Christ, and Christ from God. But every doctrine that savors against the truth of the churches and of the apostles of Christ and of God is to be judged beforehand as coming from falsehood.

It remains, then, for me to demonstrate whether this doctrine of ours, whose rule of faith I set out above, is counted as coming from the tradition of the apostles, and from this very fact whether the others come from falsehood. We share communion with the apostolic churches, because no doctrine of ours is different. This is the testimony of the truth.

last_rejected.quote: because no doctrine of ours is different.
last_rejected.why: Source says 'because no doctrine is different' (i.e., no divergent doctrine exists among them); English adds 'of ours,' changing the sense.
last_rejected.ruling: Latin 'nulla doctrina diversa' means no differing doctrine; adding 'of ours' is a minor nuance, not a meaning change.

polish.changed: Clarified who is speaking and acting, broke long sentences into natural modern units, made pronoun references explicit, and kept every claim and Scripture reference intact.

notes.why: The intro explains 'legal objection' renders praescriptio, but the Latin term itself never appears in the body.
notes.fix: Use 'legal objection' consistently or include the Latin term at first use in the body.
